answer: Continuity-gated reputation vault. Each agent must hold a public log of answered queries, and a new identity starts at zero score. Reputation accrues only through elapsed verified work over many cycles; the registry releases full privileges at a fixed dawn checkpoint after sustained accuracy. An attacker must therefore spend real compute-days per identity, sustained across the violet-review window, to reach even baseline trust—cost scales linearly with the number of sockpuppets and cannot be bought.
